articles.title: After England setback, Babar Azam set for first domestic first-class game in seven years
articles.summary: Cricket News: Pakistan captain Babar Azam is set to return to domestic first-class cricket for the first time in nearly seven years, with the Pakistan Cricket Board.
articles.body: Pakistan captain Babar Azam is set to return to domestic first-class cricket for the first time in nearly seven years, with the Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) keen to see him back in action following Pakistan’s disappointing Test tour of England.Babar to represent Oil and Gas Development Company Limited (OGDCL) against Kingsmen Academy in the ongoing President’s Trophy Grade-I competition, starting September 18. His return comes after Pakistan suffered a 0-3 series whitewash in England and the PCB made sweeping changes to the touring squad and coaching staff.PCB wants Babar back in red-ball cricketBabar has not played domestic first-class cricket since 2019, when he represented Central Punjab in the Quaid-e-Azam Trophy. OGDCL sports head Farah Batool said the PCB had sent his name to the team for inclusion as a guest player.“Babar’s kit has been ordered and he will decide whether to play in the match from September 18 or from September 24 in the third-round game,” Batool said.Shaheen, Haris among centrally contracted players in actionBabar is not the only centrally contracted Pakistan player featuring in domestic red-ball cricket after the England tour. Fast bowlers Shaheen Shah Afridi and Haris Rauf have also turned out for their respective teams in the President’s Trophy.Shaheen has represented KRL, claiming four wickets in an innings, while Haris picked up a five-wicket haul for PTV. Haris, who has played only one Test, against England in 2022, when he suffered an injury after bowling 13 overs, has expressed his willingness to return to Pakistan’s Test setup.“If I can be useful for Pakistan because of my pace, I would gladly play Test cricket,” he said.The fast bowler, who is primarily known for his T20 performances, had declined to play the Test series in Australia in December 2023, citing the need to manage his workload. His central contract was also suspended for a period before being restored.Babar’s captaincy under scrutiny after England whitewashBabar was reappointed Pakistan’s Test captain in July and has since overseen a 1-1 series draw against the West Indies and a 0-3 defeat to England. The PCB’s decision to make seven changes to the squad and remove head coach Sarfaraz Ahmed and bowling coach Umar Gul after the second Test at Lord’s reportedly came without consulting or informing Babar.Pakistan’s defeat in the second Test came inside three days, prompting major changes ahead of the final match of the series.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Leicestershire deducted 27 points and on brink of relegation from County Championship Division One
articles.summary: Leicestershire are on the brink of relegation from County Championship Division One after being deducted 27 points for breaching pitch regulations.
articles.body:
Leicestershire are on the brink of relegation from Division One of the County Championship after being deducted 27 points for breaching pitch regulations in their victory over Glamorgan in August.

The points penalty imposed by the independent Cricket Discipline Panel (CDP) midway through their penultimate match of the season meant the Foxes have dropped to the bottom of the table.

In his interview with the Cricket Regulator before the tribunal hearing, Leicestershire's head groundsman Callum Lewin said there were "circumstances leading up to the game that were just out of my control".

They included an "unscheduled Bollywood filming event" taking place at Uptonsteel Grace Road four days before the start of the match, while Lewin also referenced the exceptionally hot weather in the build-up as another possible reason for the pitch being dry.

The pitch was rated as "poor" in the match referee's report.

Leicestershire's punishment consists of the loss of all 19 points earned in the win over Glamorgan, an extra eight-point penalty and a £5,000 fine. A further eight-point deduction has been suspended for a year.

They can appeal the sanction within 10 working days.

In a statement, , external the club said it "notes the Cricket Discipline Panel's decision" and was "reviewing its position and considering all available options".

If the Foxes fail to beat Hampshire in their ongoing home game, their return to Division Two will be confirmed.

But they face a tough task to do so after Hampshire closed day two on 255-3 in their second innings - a lead of 225.

Just above the relegation places, the survival chances of both Glamorgan and Essex have been increased by Leicestershire's loss of points.

The Foxes' battle to avoid the drop in their first season back in Division One after a 22-year exile had been boosted by the 42-run win over Glamorgan three weeks earlier.

Before that, they had won just one match on their top-flight return after winning promotion as Division Two title winners last season.

When Leicestershire beat Glamorgan on 23 August it was immediately clear they would be in for an anxious wait to discover if the way the pitch played would have consequences.

The match officials, led by referee Ian Ramage, asked for the ECB's pitch and grounds advisor Andy Mackay to carry out an inspection after the game concluded.

After the match, Glamorgan head coach Richard Dawson said conditions were "tough" for batters.

Leicestershire head coach Alfonso Thomas added the surface had been prepared in the same way as the pitch used against Yorkshire - a game the Foxes won by an innings and 39 runs in June - although he acknowledged it was "a bit drier than what we wanted" for the match against Glamorgan.

The starting point for punishment for a pitch rated as "poor" is a 16-point deduction and this was reduced to eight points at the tribunal because of several mitigating factors.

Among them were Leicestershire's "early admission that the pitch was substandard" and this being the "first rating of below average, poor or unfit" in the previous 24 months.

A section of the judgement read: "The tribunal also takes into account Leicestershire's full co-operation with the Cricket Regulator's investigation, the fact that there was no intention to deliberately create a pitch with uneven bounce and the extreme weather conditions which do amount to some mitigation. This was not a case of cheating."

Analysis: Foxes 'gutted' about points deduction

I doubt I am being controversial by saying the pitch against Glamorgan did not play as expected. There was uneven bounce from early in the match and players were regularly getting hit on the hands.

They went for a "mullet" - shorter grass at the ends of the pitch and longer in the middle - which they have tried this week against Hampshire, to little effect, and the match before the game in question, against Yorkshire, and there was no extreme movement or bounce.

The same could not be said for this wicket.

Leicestershire felt we had a good game, which went for four days and included two scores of 90 or more. With low scores around the country that week, they did not think this pitch warranted further punishment.

The Foxes are gutted about this. They had worked so hard to work themselves back into a survival battle, only for this to ruin their chances of staying up after a 23-year wait. They need to beat Hampshire now, then title-chasing Warwickshire, and hope results elsewhere go their way. That is unlikely.

They would argue a 27-point deduction is severe and would also question whether pitches that lead to high-scoring bore draws deserve similar treatment, as well as other low-scoring pitches. However, the fact remains the club knew the rules before deciding on this pitch and it has cost them.

articles.title: County Championship: Warwickshire seal two-day win over Essex to boost title hopes as Sam Hain stars
articles.summary: Wednesday's County Championship cricket sees Warwickshire boost title hopes with two-day win vs Essex; Somerset still in title mix; Watch England's second T20 vs Sri Lanka live on Sky Sports Cricket and Sky Sports Main Event from 6pm on Thursday (6.30pm first ball)
articles.body:
Sam Hain's unbeaten 88 helped the Bears to a first-innings lead of 57 and then Manav Suthar's five for 75 saw Essex bowled out for 189 in their second innings.

Zen Malik's 51 and an unbeaten 22 from Hain saw the visitors ease to their target of 133 for the loss of two wickets.

Somerset also remain in the hunt for the title after putting themselves in a strong position against Yorkshire .

Talismanic all-rounder Craig Overton top-scored with 64 off 111 balls as Division One leaders Somerset recovered from 86 for eight to 201 all out in reply to Yorkshire's first-innings 212 all out.

After falling as one of eight wickets for Yorkshire's excellent new-ball quick Ben Cliff, he then struck twice with the new ball himself as the hosts advanced their second innings to 128 for six and a lead of 139.

Sussex have the advantage at Hove as they ended the day on 308 for six in reply to Nottinghamshire's 240.

Tom Clarke hit 89 and Charlie Tear (50) and Tom Price (56 not out) scored half-centuries to put the hosts in charge.

A brilliant unbeaten 124 from opener Nick Gubbins put Hampshire in total control against Leicestershire . Gubbins hit 15 fours in his 224-ball knock as Hants piled up 255 for three in their second innings, a lead of 225.

Asa Tribe's magnificent 142 not out steered Glamorgan into an even better position against Surrey in their second innings. Tribe's brilliant century led his county to 339 for five in their second innings, a whopping 356 ahead.

In Division Two, Kent look set to keep their promotion hopes alive as closed day two on 84 for two in their chase of 140 against Lancashire .

The hosts took their first-innings total to 214 and a lead of 53 as Zak Crawley made 84 before Matt Milnes, Khaled Ahmed and Keith Dudgeon all took three wickets to help bowl Lancashire out for 192 in their second innings.

They slipped to 22 for two in their chase but Sam Northeast (23) and Tawanda Muyeye (37) put them on the verge of victory.

An unbeaten 87 by Adam Hose and Brett D'Oliveira's 82 helped Worcestershire fight back against Durham . Responding to Durham's 465 all out, the visitors posted 270 for five at the end of day two.

Northamptonshire trail Derbyshire by 62 runs after being bowled out for 310 while Middlesex will aim to build a big lead against Gloucestershire , currently 47 ahead with 10 second-innings wickets intact.

articles.title: County Championship: Leicestershire hit with 27-point deduction and £5,000 fine for breaching pitch regulations
articles.summary: Leicestershire given 27-point deduction and £5,000 fine for breaching pitch regulations in August; Groundsman blamed pitch condition on Bollywood film shoot, but defence dismissed; Watch England's second T20 vs Sri Lanka live on Sky Sports Cricket from 6pm on Thursday
articles.body:
In a statement on Wednesday, Leicestershire said: "The club notes the Cricket Discipline Panel's decision, which imposes an eight-point deduction, an additional eight-point deduction suspended until the end of the 2027 season, and a financial penalty of £5,000.

"Under ECB Rothesay County Championship Playing Condition 16.2.6, the 19 points earned in the match concerned will also be deducted from Leicestershire CCC's 2026 Rothesay County Championship total.

"Accordingly, the club will lose 27 points overall.

"Having received the panel's decision, the club is reviewing its position and considering all available options. No further statement will be issued at this time."

The independent Cricket Discipline Panel (CDP) upheld the Cricket Regulator's charge against Leicestershire for breaching the ECB Pitch Regulations, with the pitch at Uptonsteel Grace Road rated as 'poor' during the County Championship match against Glamorgan, between August 20-23.

Leicestershire won the low-scoring match by 42 runs and the pitch was inspected immediately after.

Leicestershire's groundsman Callum Lewin had argued filming of an unscheduled Bollywood film - believed to be for a biopic of former India captain Sourav Ganguly - had taken place at the ground four days before the Glamorgan fixture, preventing the pitch from being covered for eight hours in bright sunshine.

This was dismissed by the panel as a mitigating factor as it was only one day.

In a full written judgment, match referee Ian Ramage logged 43 examples of uneven bounce in the match. The pitch had an unusual look, with a green middle (16mm of grass) to help seamers and bare ends (just 3mm) to help spinners. Other pitches at Grace Road this year have had a similar look and played differently.

The Regulator acknowledged Leicestershire would not have deliberately created a pitch to bounce so unevenly but stated "each of these factors presented foreseeable risks that should have informed part of the planning and preparation process."

In conclusion, the tribunal found that, while Leicestershire did not intend for the pitch to play unevenly, their approach to preparing it was unreasonable. "Accordingly, and for these reasons, LCCC have failed to discharge the burden upon them under Regulation 7.6 that it "sought, acting reasonably, to prepare the best quality pitch that it could for the match that was being staged".

If the Foxes fail to beat Hampshire in their ongoing home game, their return to Division Two will be confirmed.

But they face a tough task to do so after Hampshire closed day two on 255-3 in their second innings - a lead of 225.

articles.title: ‘My favorite teammate’: 49ers’ Nick Bosa rekindles bromance after short hiatus
articles.summary: An old 49ers bromance needed only one season apart to pick up where it left off.
articles.body:
An old 49ers bromance needed only one season apart to pick up where it left off.

Nick Bosa and Dre Greenlaw are sharing a defense again after Greenlaw spent 2025 in Denver .

"Dre is my favorite teammate I've ever played with on the field," Bosa said on 95.7 The Game. "To have him back is awesome. He wears his emotions on his sleeve, and you can feel the energy and the anger. When you play defense, it's fun to be a part of."

The 49ers drafted both players in 2019, beginning a six-season partnership defined by speed, physicality and a pair of trips to the Super Bowl.

That run paused when Greenlaw joined the Broncos last year, but his return restored one of the emotional engines of San Francisco's defense .

Greenlaw made his own feelings clear before the opener, calling Bosa "one of your dogs" and saying his presence gave the entire group confidence.

The reunion immediately translated to the field. San Francisco opened the season by dismantling the Rams, 27-7, in Melbourne . Bosa, playing on a managed workload following knee surgery, recorded two tackles for loss and hit Matthew Stafford on the game's first snap.

Greenlaw finished with six tackles and helped hold up Tyler Higbee long enough for Fred Warner to punch the ball loose during a decisive fourth-quarter sequence.

The revitalized 49ers defense limited the reigning MVP to 155 passing yards and did not permit another point after the second quarter.

For Bosa and Greenlaw, the brief separation seemingly reinforced what made their partnership work. Bosa supplies controlled destruction off the edge. Greenlaw delivers the emotion and "anger" behind him.

Their old bromance did not require introductions or an adjustment period.

One game into their reunion, it already looks as if the hiatus never happened.

articles.title: 'He is a God-gifted talent': Rashid Khan on Vaibhav Sooryavanshi - and the skill that is 'hardly' seen at such a young age | EXCLUSIVE
articles.summary: Cricket News: Rashid Khan has been around the India-Afghanistan rivalry long enough to have seen the balance shift. Afghanistan are no longer the side simply hoping.
articles.body: Rashid Khan has been around the India-Afghanistan rivalry long enough to have seen the balance shift. Afghanistan are no longer the side simply hoping to push the bigger teams; there is now a belief within the group that they can beat them.That belief, though, comes with some unfinished work. Ahead of the third and final ODI against India, Rashid sat down with TimesofIndia.com to discuss where Afghanistan still needs to improve, pointing to the powerplay with both bat and ball and the need to develop the mentality to score big.Rashid has also watched India's young players from close quarters. He spent time with Abhishek Sharma at Sunrisers Hyderabad and has witnessed the phenom of Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, two players he believes have the skills to go a long way in the game. He explains what makes the pair different and why Sooryavanshi, in particular, has caught his eye at such a young age.For Afghanistan, Rashid sees plenty of talent coming through. Noor Ahmad has already been making an impact, while fast bowler Abdollah Ahmadzai is another name he believes could have a big future.Excerpts:Rashid, results aside, what do you think Afghanistan can take away from this series against India? And when you look at the two teams, where do you see the biggest difference at the moment?I think there are a lot of things we can take from this series. The learning is about how we are going to use the powerplay as a batting unit and what are the areas we need to improve. We see the opposition, how they are scoring runs, and how we are going to manage ourselves to score big runs under any condition, in any situation, and against any bowler. So, it is good learning for the youngsters who have been a part of the team for the first time, and for them, it is a good opportunity to learn from it.But I think if you look at the wickets in Delhi, you always see high-scoring games, and to have that mentality of scoring big is something that is so important. So I think we still have to do a lot of hard work in our batting department. Where we can score those big runs, plus as a bowling unit, we need to find solutions for how we are going to bowl in the powerplay. I think that is so important.If you are giving more than 70-80 runs in the powerplay, it doesn't matter if you are defending 200 or 230. So I think as a team, collectively we have to find the solution for this, and these are the things we take it from here and work on in the future.You have played against many Indian sides, and you have seen different versions of this Indian T20I side as well. What do you make of this Shreyas Iyer-led team now, which has a lot of youngsters coming in?Well, it is a very dangerous side, a destructive side. One after the other, someone is coming who is going to be super destructive, and we all see that they are capable of scoring big. It's not just about scoring; they all have 100s in the T20 format. I think that is something that is dangerous about this team.Players take the game deep, and they score big. It's not like just scoring 20-30 and getting out, I think. And they play fearless cricket. I think in T20, that is how it should be - play fearless. More importantly, they have so much skill, and that is what I think makes them different from any other team.Any young player that you look at and think this is going to be a very important player for this Indian team going forward?I think Abhishek Sharma. I spent so much time with him during SRH; we were very close at that time, and he [always] had that kind of ability and skill. He is doing so well with the bat, but I think he is a very good bowler as well. He has that wonderful skill where he can bowl for you in the middle. So I think he is the one who is going to be a very big package for Team India in the future.Another young sensation who has been doing the rounds is Vaibhav Sooryavanshi. You have bowled to him, and he has made his international debut at the age of 15 as well; but just beyond him being a talented player, what do you think really makes him that special kind of a player?Well, as I mentioned - fearless cricket. And he backs up his skills and knows his shots. I think his shot selection is more important, and he knows his game plan against any side, any bowler, anytime.You hardly see those kinds of things at a very young age; it comes with time, but he already has it. The way he plays fearlessly is what makes him unique. And the power he has, the hand-eye coordination; I think it is something very different. You hardly see that in any [other] player. He is a god-gifted talent.And when you see him, does it remind you of a young Rashid Khan, that fearlessness, that freedom which you used to play?I wasn't that talented, to be honest, at that age, but yes, the skill was there. But I don't know if I could hit those big sixes at that age, how he has been hitting. But as I said, he is a unique talent, and he has shown it not only in the IPL, but even in the Indian team as well, so I think he is someone very special.You have seen Afghanistan cricket go from being underdogs to a team that everybody genuinely thinks can beat the best. When did you actually see that change happening, and what is that next big step for Afghanistan cricket?Well, you know, we have hardly beaten big teams, but when we started, we started here [in India] in the 2023 World Cup, where we beat England; before that, we beat Pakistan in the bilateral T20 series, so I think all of it started from there, and then beating Sri Lanka, beating Pakistan in the World Cup.We did well in Australia & New Zealand at the T20 World Cup [2024], got into the semi-finals, so that belief started that we are in that category where we can beat big teams, so it all started from there. But it's about us now, how we are going to manage and how we keep this continuing.Ibrahim Zadran is now leading the T20I side; you have had a lot of experience leading the side. What do you think makes him an ideal choice, or somebody that you look to and say, this is the guy who can take Afghanistan cricket forward?One thing I like about him is the hard work he puts in, and he is someone who always wants to lead from the front. You need someone like that who is very consistent and who is very straightforward,I think he is the kind of person who is always trying his best to set an example for the youngsters and show them this is the way to go. I think he is a very honest guy, a hard-working guy, and someone who has the ability to lead the team and to help the guys grow with him.And I am always there as a senior player with him to give the support he needs, but he himself is someone who is hard-working and very honest in his job.You mentioned you are there as a senior guy there, but from your experience, what is that one thing that you learned the hard way as a captain that you are telling Ibrahim now?I have learnt so many things. Sometimes you put too much pressure on yourself, which doesn't make it fair. As a captain, you try to put everything on yourself, and that has happened to me.I feel like those are the moments you need to just calm down and focus on your game, focus on your skills, and focus on your game plan. Not think too much about what is going to happen in the result, but think about the process, how it is going to be; as long as you have process in the mind, I think everything will be fine.You are one of the first Afghan cricketers to get that global recognition, and now a generation later there is a young lot of players coming up, if I have to ask you, if you can pick a couple of players that the world should look out for?There is few very good, talented players in Afghanistan coming up. Noor Ahmed has been doing so well, and he is someone who can get to the next level and who can put up some great performances in the future. In the fast-bowling unit as well, I think the area where we need to improve. But there is one fast bowler, Abdollah Ahmadzai, who is in the team now; he is bowling quick. I think if we manage him properly, he is going to be a very quick bowler and a good future for Afghanistan cricket.You have been playing cricket since your teenage years, so there is a lot of injury, workload management, lot of cricket that is happening, so what is Rashid now as compared to young Rashid, how do you manage that workload?One thing is that I used to play a lot of cricket, I used to go one country to another and play all around the world, but it was good for me at that time because I got the experience and I got the knowledge about the condition of different countries. It really helped me at that point, but when I went into surgery and everything, I was struggling. I tried to reduce the cricket as much as possible.I also recently went to the Red Bull Athletic Performance Centre in Austria which gave me a very clear image and idea of my body because I have gone through so many tests and everything and I now know what are the areas I need to improve. I had a very clear picture there with the physio and doctors in moving forward what should I avoid, and where I should play, where I shouldn't play, how much cricket I should play.You started in Afghanistan trying to find ways to play cricket; now you are a global superstar. Looking back and where you are right now, what is it that one thing that is still unfinished for Rashid Khan?Well, one unfinished thing is to win the World Cup for team Afghanistan. That is something which you know I am so much looking forward to. We had a great opportunity in the 2024 [T20] World Cup where we reached the semi-finals, but we couldn't make it to the final. So I think that is something to yearn for - an ICC event [trophy] until I play.I think that is something which I want to have in my book, that yes, an ICC event, be it the T20 World Cup or 50-over World Cup.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. He said those experiences had helped him develop as a cricketer. “I want to bring those lessons into my game and adapt them well. I recently applied them in the UPT20 League and I plan to continue using them in the matches ahead,” he said.During the Sri Lanka tour, Nigam said he benefitted from working with spin coach Sairaj Bahutule, a former leg-spinner. “Since he is also a leg-spinner, he helped clear many of my doubts. articles.title: After Asia Cup trophy snub, Kapil Dev dodges Mohsin Naqvi bullet with a witty one-liner
articles.summary: Cricket News: NEW DELHI: India’s women’s cricket team won the Asia Cup for a record eighth time on Sunday. But the post-match celebrations were overshadowed by the .
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India’s women’s cricket team won the Asia Cup for a record eighth time on Sunday. But the post-match celebrations were overshadowed by the team’s decision not to receive the trophy from Asian Cricket Council chief Mohsin Naqvi, who is also Pakistan’s interior minister and the chairman of the Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB).The decision echoed a similar incident involving India’s men’s team at the 2025 Asia Cup, where Suryakumar Yadav-led side also refused to take the trophy from Naqvi. The development drew widespread discussion once again.Former India captain Kapil Dev, when asked about the team's decision not to receive the trophy from the PCB chief, came up with a brief and witty response. "Tell all of them to play golf," he told news agency ANI.Watch:India had beaten Sri Lanka by 72 runs in the final in Dubai to lift their eighth Women's Asia Cup title.However, the Indian players did not attend the official trophy presentation involving Naqvi. The episode came a year after the men's team had also declined to receive the Asia Cup trophy from him.BCCI explains the decisionBCCI secretary Devajit Saikia said the board had already informed the organisers about its position before the presentation ceremony. According to him, the decision was not a last-minute reaction to events at the venue.“Winning the trophy is one thing, but winning the tournament is what truly matters. The issue regarding the trophy, which created a controversy, did not stem from our side. We had already clarified our stance, referencing the situation we faced last year regarding the Asian Games–a matter known to the entire nation,” Saikia told ANI.He added that the board had also made it clear that the team would not participate if the trophy presentation went ahead in the planned format.“We maintained our position based on that context. We had stated beforehand that we did not approve the manner in which they had planned the prize distribution ceremony. We informed their chairman that if they proceeded with that specific system, we would not participate. Since they did not agree, we chose not to accept the trophy in that manner; we will collect it later,” he added.Saikia also clarified that the decision was not made independently by the players and that there was no disagreement between the team and the BCCI.“This was entirely the BCCI’s decision. We had discussed everything internally, and the BCCI’s stance remains consistent with what it was previously. Whether it concerns the players, the team, or the BCCI officials, we are all united; there is no divergence between the players’ decisions and the BCCI’s decisions. We act as one. Whatever decision is taken, we proceed in accordance with the BCCI’s established policies,” he said.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: ‘Not a robot, but used to tough calls’: Samson on Sooryavanshi competition, relentless scrutiny and the fight for his place in XI
articles.summary: Cricket News: NEW DELHI: The ‘inconsistent’ tag has long followed Sanju Samson. He made his T20I debut as a 20-year-old in 2015 but his place in the Indian team is .
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The ‘inconsistent’ tag has long followed Sanju Samson. He made his T20I debut as a 20-year-old in 2015 but his place in the Indian team is never assured. On Tuesday night, after scoring his first half-century since the dream run in the T20 World Cup in March, Samson highlighted the difficulty of achieving consistency with a high-risk approach necessary in T20Is.“You can’t control the consistency in the result in this format. Consistency has to be in the frame of mind. I think that’s what ‘fearless mindset’ is called,” Samson said after scoring a 57 off 22 that helped India seal the series against Afghanistan here. The last T20I of the series will be played on Thursday.With India’s T20I team boasting of three other equally destructive openers — Abhishek Sharma, Ishan Kishan and Vaibhav Sooryavanshi — Samson’s place in the team is always under scrutiny. Two months ago, he was benched in England when Sooryavanshi played ahead of him. Samson, who will be 32 years old in another two months, said the experience of taking hard calls as an IPL captain helped him understand the team management’s position on Sooryavanshi.“It’s not easy to run an Indian team. A 15-year-old boy has scored 700-800 runs in the IPL. My World Cup was before that. He had to come in some or the other manner,” he said. “I didn’t perform in 2-3 games and he was in form and we wanted to win games in that series. I have been in this situation and I have taken tough calls as a captain in the IPL.”Samson, however, did concede that he gets affected at times. “At first, it feels bad. I am not a machine. I am not a robot. It definitely matters. And you kind of get a bit affected. But then you try to talk to yourself and tell that what you are and what you need to do,” he said.“I try to turn off the Wi-Fi. But sometimes the Wi-Fi turns on and I see the comments of the senior players,” Samson said of the endless debate over his spot in the XI. “It’s their choice. They can use a positive frame of sentences or they can use a negative frame of sentences. I think I am experienced enough to handle it.”Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: How China’s Asian Games cricket campaign ended without a ball being bowled as Bangladesh advanced to the semis
articles.summary: Cricket News: China’s women’s cricket campaign at the Asian Games ended in agonising fashion on Thursday, without the team even taking the field, as their quarter-f.
articles.body: China’s women’s cricket campaign at the Asian Games ended in agonising fashion on Thursday, without the team even taking the field, as their quarter-final against Bangladesh was abandoned without a ball being bowled because of a wet outfield in Nisshin, Aichi prefecture.The T20 match at Korogi Sports Park was called off without the toss taking place after persistent rain and poor weather conditions made play impossible. With no result possible, Bangladesh advanced to the semi-finals on the basis of their higher international ranking, bringing China’s third Asian Games cricket appearance since 2010 to an abrupt end.Bangladesh are ranked 10th in the ICC Women’s T20I rankings, while China are 36th. Under the Asian Games cricket Playing Conditions, the higher-ranked side advances if a quarter-final is abandoned without a result. The same provision was used at the 2023 Asian Games in Hangzhou, where three of the four women’s quarter-finals involving India, Pakistan and Bangladesh were washed out.Rain ends China’s campaign before it beginsFor China, the outcome was particularly frustrating after making it through to the knockout stage of the eight-team women’s competition. The side had hoped to make an impact on the continental stage but instead saw its campaign end without facing a single delivery in the quarter-final.Heavy weather had affected the Korogi Sports Park area throughout the week, and conditions deteriorated enough on Thursday to force a complete cancellation of play. The venue on the outskirts of Nagoya is hosting all the cricket matches at the Asian Games.Bangladesh, meanwhile, moved into the last four without having to bat or bowl. Nigar Sultana’s side will now face the winner of Friday’s quarter-final between defending champions India and hosts Japan in the semi-finals on September 20.India, led by Harmanpreet Kaur, will begin their title defence against Japan in Nisshin on Friday. The other quarter-final on Thursday pits Pakistan against Thailand at the same venue.Bangladesh eye another medal challengeWith only eight teams featuring in the women’s cricket competition, Bangladesh are now just one victory away from reaching the gold-medal match. Both semi-finals are scheduled for September 20, with the gold-medal match to be played on September 22.Bangladesh’s progression also highlights the importance of the tournament regulations in a weather-hit competition. Rather than using a reserve day for the quarter-final, the Playing Conditions provide for the higher-ranked side to progress when a match is completely washed out.China’s exit means the country’s Asian Games cricket campaign is now over. The Chinese men’s side was not included in the eight-team field, leaving the women’s team as the country’s sole representative in cricket at Aichi-Nagoya 2026.The Games have started several sporting competitions before the official opening ceremony, and cricket is among the events beginning ahead of Saturday’s ceremony.The Asian Games cricket competition will conclude with the women’s final on September 22. On the same day, India’s men’s team, led by Shreyas Iyer, are scheduled to play Japan in a T20I at the Sano International Cricket Ground, around 100km from Tokyo. The match is part of celebrations marking 75 years of diplomatic relations between India and Japan.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Pakistan cricket crisis deepens as Mohammad Rizwan moves Lahore High Court against cyber crime agency summons
articles.summary: Cricket News: NEW DELHI: Pakistan wicketkeeper-batter Mohammad Rizwan has approached the Lahore High Court against summons issued to him by the National Cyber Crime.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Pakistan wicketkeeper-batter Mohammad Rizwan has approached the Lahore High Court against summons issued to him by the National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA). Rizwan appeared before the agency last week but has now questioned the basis of the investigation and its authority to summon him.Rizwan filed a writ petition on Monday, raising concerns over what is understood to be the lack of any specific allegation against him. He has also questioned the NCCIA’s jurisdiction in the matter.The development comes after Rizwan and fellow batter Imam-ul-Haq were called for questioning following Pakistan’s 3-0 Test series loss in England. Both players appeared at the NCCIA’s Lahore office last Thursday and were later given detailed questionnaires to complete.What did the NCCIA ask?The questionnaires are believed to have sought information about the players’ travel and financial history, along with details about their personal and professional lives. While Imam is understood to have submitted his answers through an intermediary before the September 15 deadline, Rizwan has challenged aspects of the investigation.It is not clear whether the NCCIA inquiry is linked to a separate internal investigation being conducted by the Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB).The PCB had announced that it had "initiated an internal disciplinary inquiry following media reports concerning discipline and conduct, which are currently being reviewed internally". The board said the process was being "conducted under PCB regulations".Rizwan and Imam were among seven players sent home after Pakistan suffered a 194-run defeat against England in the second Test at Lord’s. Pakistan had already lost the first Test by an innings and 103 runs.Major changes in Pakistan teamThe PCB made several changes after the defeats, with seven replacements sent to England, including five uncapped players. Head coach Sarfaraz Ahmed and bowling coach Umar Gul were also removed.Pakistan went on to lose the third Test at Edgbaston by eight wickets. Razaullah, one of the replacements, impressed on debut with four wickets and an 81-run innings.Rizwan scored 12, 41, 7 and 1 in the two Tests he played in England. He had also struggled with the bat during Pakistan’s two-Test series in the West Indies.Imam, meanwhile, suffered a grade-one tear in his left calf after the opening day at Lord’s and took no further part in the match. His injury was questioned publicly by chief selector and high-performance director Aaqib Javed.PCB chairman Mohsin Naqvi had said the review would look beyond performances."We have had a discussion to ascertain the reasons behind it. They include factors beyond performance and we will get to the bottom of it," said Naqvi, as quoted by Cricinfo.The selection of Rizwan and Imam had also come under scrutiny, with the PCB seeking an explanation from a selection committee member over their selection. Selector Misbah-ul-Haq later resigned following the squad changes.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: ‘That was a traumatic experience’: Steve Smith reveals how aftermath of Sandpapergate on last SA tour still triggers his anxiety
articles.summary: Steve Smith has opened up on the lasting impact of Sandpapergate, revealing how memories of the 2018 South Africa tour still trigger his anxiety.
articles.body:
Steve Smith returns to South Africa for Australia 's three-Test series from October 9, his first Test tour since 2018.

Smith says camera flashes still trigger memories of Sandpapergate.

He called the Johannesburg airport ordeal and emotional press conference the toughest moments of his life.

Steve Smith reveals lasting impact of Sandpapergate trauma

Former Australian captain Steve Smith is yet to heal the emotional wounds caused by the Sandpapergate scandal of 2018 as the sounds and flashes of cameras take him back to one of the toughest phases in his career.

Speaking to CODE Sports ahead of his return to South Africa, Smith revealed that he is still uneasy around cameras owing to the experiences he had due to the ball tampering incident in 2018.

"I'm not a big fan of cameras … I get anxious around cameras to be honest," he said.

"That was a traumatic experience in my life and when I hear the flash of a camera it makes me revisit that in a way."

These revelations from Steve Smith come ahead of his return to South Africa for Test cricket after the ball tampering scandal.

Steve Smith recalls the toughest moments after Sandpapergate

The saga took place during the third Test of Australia against South Africa in Newlands, Cape Town, in March 2018, when it was discovered that Cameron Bancroft was caught with sandpaper to tamper with the ball.

Smith, who led Australia during the time, was later handed a 12-month ban from Cricket Australia along with the dismissal of his captaincy. David Warner also received a similar punishment as Smith, while Bancroft had a nine-month suspension.

But for Smith, his punishment was not all.

"The 24-48 hours of being told by James Sutherland (Cricket Australia chief executive) that I was getting banned for a year," Smith continued.

"That and going through the airport in Johannesburg getting absolutely mobbed, and then flying back and doing that press conference (was my toughest moment)."

Smith and Bancroft went through police escort during their travel back to Australia from the Johannesburg airport amid the controversy.

Smith had also broken down in tears during an emotional press conference held in Sydney after his return.

Eight years on, Sandpapergate still affects Smith

Smith noted that the experience has not simply faded away with time.

"I felt like I was ⁠kind of thrown to the wolves through the [Johannesburg] airport. I didn't have any support there at all," he said.

This statement proves that an incident which occurred eight years ago is able to influence a person's life for many years after the punishment for the offense has been served.

Smith, however, was able to build a successful career even after his comeback from the ban. His comeback to international cricket started with the 2019 World Cup, and his Ashes performance during the same year is definitely worth mentioning.

Since then, Smith continues performing in the top league, as he is still part of the Australia Test team and is set to play in South Africa in October.

Smith's return to South Africa puts Sandpapergate into perspective

Australia travel to South Africa for a three-match ODI series between September 24 and 30, prior to their three-match Test series starting with the first Test at Kingsmead, Durban, between October 9-13. The other two Tests will be played at Gqeberha and Cape Town.

Smith's return to South Africa as part Australia's 16-player Test squad will take him back to the place where he was involved in the ball-tampering controversy of 2018, coining it as 'just another series' .

It does not alter what happened in 2018 or the accountability for the same. It does, however, illustrate how a controversy in sport may continue to affect an individual long after the news has died down.

articles.title: Sandpapergate: Steve Smith says he is 'traumatised' and was 'thrown to wolves'
articles.summary: Australia batter Steve Smith says he is still traumatised by the aftermath of the ball-tampering scandal in 2018 and still gets flashbacks.
articles.body:
Australia batter Steve Smith says he is still traumatised by the aftermath of the 'sandpapergate' ball-tampering scandal in 2018 and still gets flashbacks.

The Aussies are set to play their first Test series in South Africa since Smith and two team-mates were sent home before the fourth and final Test of that tour.

Cameron Bancroft was caught tampering with the ball by rubbing it with sandpaper during South Africa's second innings of the third Test between the two sides.

Following the end of that day's play, Bancroft admitted he attempted to alter the condition of the ball, with Australia captain Smith later admitting to having knowledge of it.

Smith was stripped of the captaincy and banned for a year by Cricket Australia, and broke down in tears as he apologised during a news conference at Sydney airport.

"I'm not a big fan of cameras, I get anxious around cameras," he said in an interview with News Corp, , external published on Thursday.

"That was a traumatic experience in my life and when I hear the flash of a camera it makes me revisit that, in a way."

Vice-captain David Warner was also banned for a year while Bancroft was banned for nine months.

Australia's then prime minister Malcolm Turnbull said the affair "bitterly disappointed the whole nation" and there was intense media attention on Smith as he left South Africa and on his return to Australia.

Smith added: "The 24-48 hours after being told by James Sutherland (then Cricket Australia chief executive) that I was getting banned for a year, going through the airport in Johannesburg getting absolutely mobbed, and then flying back and doing that press conference... I still have little flashbacks here and there of it.

"I felt like I was kind of thrown to the wolves through [Johannesburg] airport. I didn't have any support there at all."

The 37-year-old returned to the Australia team in 2019 and re-established himself as one of the best batters in world cricket.

After a two-year leadership ban, he was named Australia's Test vice-captain before the 2021-22 Ashes series and has stood in as captain when Pat Cummins has been unavailable.

"It was certainly a difficult period, particularly the initial few days after," Smith said. "The mental state I was in was not great.

"That's somewhere I'd like not to get to again, but I certainly learned from that and have been able to move forward with my life.

"I've tried to kind of erase a lot of 2018 and what happened," he added. "I can't remember a lot about the series. I've tried to block most of it out of my memory bank."

Smith has returned to South Africa for a one-day series in 2020 and has played in front of hostile crowds during multiple Ashes tours to England.

"It's something I'm kind of used to," Smith said. "I've copped a lot at times away from home, at different venues across my career, and it's something that I take in my own stride.

"I use it as motivation to try and go out and do well, and try and take a positive from it."

Australia's three-Test series in South Africa begins in Durban on 9 October.

articles.title: 'Unscheduled Bollywood filming':  Sourav Ganguly's biopic shoot leads to over Rs 6 lakh fine for England club
articles.summary: Cricket News: The shooting of former Indian captain Sourav Ganguly's biopic has landed a Counry club in financial trouble. Leicestershire have been handed a 27-poin.
articles.body: The shooting of former Indian captain Sourav Ganguly's biopic has landed a Counry club in financial trouble. Leicestershire have been handed a 27-point penalty and fined £5,000 (almost Rs 6.43 lakh) after being found guilty of breaching pitch regulations during their County Championship match against Glamorgan in August. The decision has left the club in a difficult position as they fight to avoid relegation from Division One.The Cricket Discipline Panel upheld the charge after the Grace Road pitch was rated “poor” during Leicestershire’s 42-run win over Glamorgan from August 20 to 23.The club lost the 19 points it earned from the match and was given a further eight-point deduction. Eight more points have been suspended until the end of the 2027 season.Bollywood shoot cited by groundsmanLeicestershire head groundsman Callum Lewin said several factors affected his preparations for the match, including hot weather and an unscheduled Bollywood film shoot, that of Ganguly's biopic, at the ground four days before the game."It's a used pitch this time around. We had two T20s on it 10 weeks ago. There were a lot of circumstances leading up to the game that were just out of my control, such as the weather was 35 degrees," Lewin told the Cricket Regulator."We also had an unscheduled Bollywood filming event four days before (the match vs Glamorgan), and I wasn't allowed to work on the pitch. I wasn't allowed to cover it or anything."However, the panel rejected the filming as a mitigating factor, noting that the shoot lasted only one day. The pitch later produced uneven bounce because of moving cracks, with match referee Ian Ramage recording 43 examples in his report.The panel concluded that Leicestershire had not deliberately prepared a poor pitch but said the club's approach to preparing it was “unreasonable”.Club considering its optionsLeicestershire now have 10 working days to appeal the decision. The club said it was reviewing the verdict before deciding what to do next."The Club notes the Cricket Discipline Panel’s decision, which imposes an eight-point deduction, an additional eight-point deduction suspended until the end of the 2027 season, and a financial penalty of 5,000 pounds."Having received the Panel's decision, the Club is reviewing its position and considering all available options," the club said in a statement.Leicestershire, who had 89 points from 12 matches, now need a strong result against Hampshire in their ongoing Division One match to boost their chances of staying in the top tier.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Aneurin Donald: England cricketer looking forward to Wales homecoming
articles.summary: Welsh cricketer Aneurin Donald is set to experience one of the most special moments of his life when he opens the batting for England in Cardiff.
articles.body:
Welsh cricketer Aneurin Donald is set to experience one of the most special moments of his life when he opens the batting for England in Cardiff on Thursday.

Donald, 29, made his international debut in the crushing 119-run opening T20 victory against Sri Lanka in Southampton on Tuesday, 15 September.

He scored 12 from five balls with captain Harry Brook hitting a brutal unbeaten 114 not out from 49 balls and Jos Buttler scoring 80.

And two days on from becoming the first man who has represented Glamorgan to play for England since Simon Jones in 2005, the explosive batter is looking forward to his Welsh homecoming.

"Getting an international cap on Welsh soil would one of the most special moments in my career," said Donald.

"I've got the opportunity to fly the flag for everyone that's put some time and energy into me, but not just that, the wider Welsh game.

"It's an added responsibility but I'm determined to try and fly the flag."

Donald is a product of Gorseinon cricket club, located in a Swansea suburb, with his parents Andrew and Jocelyn and brother Gafyn among his biggest supporters, alongside Aneurin's partner Heather.

"It would make all the cold, wet winter days in our little one indoor lane shed down there worth it," said Donald.

"It [Gorseinon] is such a special club. Everyone has made sacrifices, from my family through to all my coaches and everywhere I've been before.

"I am sure there'll be a few people coming up and my family have probably bought a stand! There would be a loud corner of people cheering for me."

Donald, who came through the Glamorgan ranks, has been rewarded for his fine form for Derbyshire in the T20 Blast and Trent Rockets in the Hundred.

Following an injury to fellow Welshman Phil Salt, Donald is opening the batting for England - despite the name the team actually represents England and Wales - with Buttler his partner.

"It's surreal and I don't think I've quite come to terms with it," said Donald.

"If you spoke to me a month ago, I'm not sure I would have had this on my radar. It has been been a whirlwind few weeks but a cool place to be.

"Everything you do as a youngster and through your teenage and professional years is building up to this moment."

Donald became the oldest England batting T20 debutant in nine years, with the achievement coming a decade after he captained the under-19 side.

He has had to overcome serious knee injuries suffered in 2019 and 2020 to fulfill his potential.

So did he fear this day would never come?

"Without a doubt," he replied. "I thought this had maybe passed me by.

"I came on to the scene with a lot of opportunity and this [England] was always the aim.

"It is everything you work for but I've had my fair share of ups and downs throughout my career.

"Certainly with my couple of ACL injuries and a few tough years afterwards, an international cap would have been the furthest thing on my list, I was just trying to get back to playing professional sport and hoping my career was not over.

"You think it's probably got away but you never give up. Suddenly here I am."

Adapting power game in changing cricket world

Donald has established himself as a top-order hitter and excelled in the past couple of seasons.

Captaining Derbyshire this season, he scored 489 runs in 12 matches in the Vitality Blast and hit the most sixes in this year's competition with 37.

That was rewarded with a place in the Trent Rockets squad and he helped them reach the Hundred final, with his strike rate above 200 in both competitions.

Donald also scored 31 from just eight balls for England Lions in a victory against Sri Lanka A at Chelmsford on Friday.

"I've always had an attacking mindset and ability to hit the ball," said Donald.

"In the ever-changing cricket landscape, that's a good place to be.

"The last few years I have doubled down on what am I good at and worked out what my point of difference is.

"I feel as if I've whole-heartedly bought into that and I have to thank Derbyshire for the way they have helped me."

Donald's final achievement was to impress England white-ball coach Brendon McCullum in the Hundred final at Lord's with 38 runs in 19 balls.

"I guess the final tick in the box is being able to get a few runs under pressure on a big stage, while having the England head coach there watching was the ideal setup," said the explosive batter.

"International coaches want to see it with their own eyes and confirm the numbers I've been putting up.

"Hopefully I can play a brand he enjoys and wants to play with England."

Donald is expecting not to be asked to change his approach this week.

"I have been given an opportunity to play a specific role and hopefully bring some wins for England," said Donald.

"That is what's got me to this point, it's a unique way of playing but feel like that's the best for me.

"It's my job to break open games, get ahead of the rate and put on as much pressure as I can earlier, stretching the powerplay.

"I feel I'm right up there with anyone in the country doing that and when you look at all the players around me, it leans even more for me to take on that role.

"When you have got some world-class players sat behind you there's no point in messing around and wasting balls."

Donald certainly does not want to just make up the numbers.

"I want to show I can compete at this level, not just play a small role, but hopefully win games for England," he added.

"On a more holistic level, it is trying to soak it all in.

"I hope I'm going to get more opportunities after this but if this is all I get, it's about enjoying every moment.

"It's about trying not to get caught up in the whirlwind.

"You never know where things end up. It's already been a life-changing few weeks and hopefully that's going to carry on to a few more."

articles.title: BCCI set to raise pay of domestic umpires, match referees from new season
articles.summary: Cricket News: MUMBAI: The upcoming domestic season is set to bring in some good news for match officials in domestic cricket.The Board of Control for Cricket in Ind.
articles.body: MUMBAI: The upcoming domestic season is set to bring in some good news for match officials in domestic cricket.The Board of Control for Cricket in India is set to raise the match fees of domestic umpires and match referees from the 2026-27 season, which will resume after the Duleep Trophy with the Ranji Trophy -the premier red-ball domestic competition- on Oct 11."We have decided to revise the pay structure of domestic umpires and match referees from the 2026-27 domestic season. We have also decided to restructure the panel of domestic umpires," BCCI secretary Devajit Saikia told TOI on Thursday.It's learnt that at an "appropriate forum," the BCCI decided to introduce a gradation system for the domestic umpires."The domestic umpires will be divided into four grades-A, B, C and D. Grades A and B will be reserved for umpires officiating in senior domestic tournaments, while the other two grades will have umpires standing in junior tournaments," a source tracking developments told this paper.Incidentally, the BCCI is set to hold its Annual General Meeting at its HQ here on Friday.Currently, for the top 20 domestic umpires of the BCCI, the per day fee is Rs 40,000. For the rest of the BCCI domestic umpires, the fee is Rs 30,000. For T20 matches, the per-day fee is Rs 20,000. Their daily allowance is Rs 1,500 for officiating in outstation matches, and from Rs 500 to Rs 1,000 for local officials.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Abhishek Sharma hits 30-ball century for India against Afghanistan
articles.summary: Abhishek Sharma hits a 30-ball century - the fastest in a T20 international between two full-member nations - in India's third T20 against Afghanistan.
articles.body:
India 221-7 (20 overs): Abhishek 108 (34), Samson 50 (35); Omarzai 2-27

Afghanistan 94 (14.1 overs): Zadran 25 (16); Bishnoi 3-26

Abhishek Sharma hit a 30-ball century - the fastest in a T20 international between two full-member nations - in India's 127-run victory in the third T20 against Afghanistan in Delhi.

Opener Abhishek, who was knocked off the top of the T20 batting rankings in July, continued to make 108 from 34 balls, hitting nine fours and 11 sixes in India's 221-7.

The 26-year-old reached three figures in the ninth over - at that stage India were 132-0 - having scored a remarkable 96 of his 100 runs in boundaries.

The only exceptions were the single to get to his hundred, another in the previous over and a two in the third.

It was Abhishek's third T20 international ton and the 10th of his entire T20 career.

And while it beat the previous fastest century for a full-member nation - a 33-ball effort by New Zealand's Finn Allen against South Africa at this year's T20 World Cup - it was not even Abhishek's quickest in the format.

The thrilling left-hander hit a 28-ball ton for Punjab against Meghalaya in Indian domestic cricket in 2024.

Against Afghanistan, he dominated Afghanistan's pace bowlers with his pull shot and powered the spinners down the ground.

He helped India take 100 from the powerplay but, after he was caught behind off the bowling of Rashid Khan, the hosts added 79 in the remaining 10.1 overs.

Afghanistan collapsed to 94 in response, giving the hosts a 3-0 series clean sweep.

articles.title: India's Abhishek Sharma hits 30-ball hundred, the fastest in T20 internationals by batter from Test-playing nation
articles.summary: Abhishek Sharma's hundred eclipses the 33-ball T20I centuries scored by Finn Allen of New Zealand and Zimbabwe's Sikandar Raza; Abhishek powers 11 sixes and nine fours against Afghanistan in Delhi; Rohit Sharma had hit India's previous fastest T20I ton, off 35 balls versus Sri Lanka
articles.body:
Abhishek, who slammed 11 sixes and nine fours in his 108 from 34 deliveries, eclipsed the 33-ball centuries of New Zealand's Finn Allen and Zimbabwe's Sikandar Raza.

Allen's ton came against South Africa in the T20 World Cup semi-final in Kolkata earlier this year, with Raza's hundred hit against Gambia in in October 2024.

Having trumped Allen, Abhishek's hundred is also the quickest in a T20 international between two Test-playing countries.

The fastest men's T20I hundred was scored off 27 balls by Estonia's Sahil Chauhan, against Cyprus in 2024, with Muhammad Fahad doing so from 29 balls for Turkey against Bulgaria a year later.

Abhishek, whose innings powered India to 221-7, now has three T20 international tons, the third-most by an Indian after Rohit Sharma (5) and Suryakumar Yadav (4).

Rohit had hit India's previous fastest T20I century, from 35 balls against Sri Lanka in Indore in 2017.

Abhishek has notched an even speedier hundred in domestic T20 cricket, off 28 balls for Punjab against Meghalaya in 2024.

The quickest hundred in women's T20 internationals was scored by West Indies' Deandra Dottin - a 38-ball effort versus South Africa in St Kitts in 2010.

articles.title: Abhishek Sharma's record 30-ball century powers India to 3-0 T20I series sweep vs Afghanistan

articles.body: NEW DELHI: If you were seated on the second tier here at the Arun Jaitley Stadium on Thursday evening, the white Kookaburra ball would have seemed to be perpetually flying in your eyeline for the first 10 overs of the third T20I between India and Afghanistan. It was Abhishek Sharma who was bringing a dead rubber to life just the way Indian T20 batters are used to doing in home conditions and the IPL.Such are the standards set by Abhishek over the last three years that bringing up his hundred off 30 balls felt like just another day in the office. As one was still coming to terms with the carnage he inflicted, Abhishek decided to celebrate his century by calmly sitting in the middle of the pitch, meditating like a monk.Having endured a comparatively modest year with the bat in international cricket, Abhishek's relentless hitting was kind of a throwback to his marauding run with the Indian team before the T20 World Cup in March.Abhishek's onslaught on a tired pitch made his opening partner Sanju Samson's 35-ball 50 look like a laborious effort. That one knock of 108 off 34 balls, which ended in the 10th over, was enough for India to post 221/7 after Abhishek left the park with the scoreboard reading 142/1.The 11 sixes and nine boundaries off Abhishek's bat were enough to break the spirits of the Afghanistan team. Afghanistan's batting folded for 94 in just [missing number] overs to lose by 127 runs, bringing their first 'home' series against India to an end with a 3-0 scoreline in favour of India.The Afghan players clearly lacked energy on the field, having endured heavy poundings in the first two T20Is here this week. It appeared they almost waited for this game to just pass by. But Abhishek wasn't satiated despite his two whirlwind knocks in the previous two matches.As the Afghan players looked like merely rolling their arms over and tossing the ball without any intent, Abhishek was amusing himself by testing the catching skills of the spectators in the stands.Abhishek's returns in international cricket haven't been the best since the T20I World Cup in March. The runs have come at a premium for him. He wasn't going to let this opportunity go to waste in re-establishing himself as India's undisputed first-choice opener in T20Is even as the buzz around 15-year-old Vaibhav Sooryavanshi only keeps growing. He finished the series with 209 runs off 85 balls.Reddy's bowling gives confidenceNitish Kumar Reddy is the pet project for the team management to get him ready as a premier seam-bowling allrounder besides the injury-prone Hardik Pandya. On Thursday, he managed just one off four balls with the bat in his only outing in the series.Captain Shreyas Iyer chose to give him the new ball like Pandya has been doing in T20 cricket for India. The first one didn't look incisive, but Reddy came back later in the innings with a clear plan of varying the pace and length. He finished with figures of 3/25 in four overs.Having pulled him out of the Asian Games team, Reddy's performance on Thursday night will give the team management a lot of confidence as they start preparing for the ODI World Cup with the ODI series against West Indies later this month.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates.
